# Concurrent transactions: protect an invariant and recover safely

[← All question groups](../index.md) · `sql-transactions-concurrency` · **SQL Server & Data Engineering** · Catalog level: senior

<p>Questions come from the preserved source notes. Reframing, assessment intent, senior signals and rubrics are editorial interpretations, not verified model answers or universal interviewer expectations. Follow-ups and the combined production exercise are agent additions. Reading this bank creates no learning record, score, completion or review schedule.</p>

## Start with one representative question

[S03-Q019](#S03-Q019)

<p>For competing updates to the same business record, how would you choose between optimistic concurrency and pessimistic locking?</p>

## One group objective and observable capabilities

<p>Defend a concurrency-control choice and its recovery behavior for a shared-data invariant.</p>

<ul>
<li>Trace commit/rollback and conflicting interleavings against an explicit invariant.</li>
<li>Compare locking, optimistic control and versioned isolation within the actual database configuration.</li>
<li>Reconstruct a deadlock cycle and justify prevention plus bounded application recovery.</li>
</ul>

**Prerequisites**

No catalog prerequisite. Establish the terms and scenario assumptions in the foundation questions before progressing; a published lesson is not evidence that you know them.

<p>Would optimistic concurrency or pessimistic locking fit two competing updates? Begin with the state changes that the business permits, then examine what overlapping readers and writers may observe. Deadlock questions extend that model from normal contention to a wait cycle, diagnosis and safe recovery; transaction presence alone does not answer the concurrency requirement.</p>

<a id="S03-Q017"></a>

### S03-Q017 · Foundation

<p>What does a database transaction protect, and what happens to its changes on commit or rollback? Trace a two-step update.</p>

**Source:** [S03-Q017](../../sources/03-sql-data-performance.md#q017)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S03-Q017](../../sources/03-sql-data-performance.md#q017)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain transactions and commit/rollback behavior.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Use an operation with a clear consistency rule. Explain the state visible after success and after a failure between the steps.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Reason about a local transaction&#x27;s state changes and failure boundary.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Assume one SQL Server database and an explicit transaction. External requests and messages are outside that transaction unless a separate mechanism is stated.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>States an invariant and traces both successful and interrupted execution.</li>
<li>Separates database atomicity from uncertainty at the caller or effects outside the database.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Claiming rollback undoes external calls or treating a caller timeout as proof of rollback.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would you investigate a timeout that occurs while the caller waits for commit?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S03-Q018"></a>

### S03-Q018 · Foundation

<p>What changes when multiple database operations overlap in time? Use two requests that access the same business data.</p>

**Source:** [S03-Q018](../../sources/03-sql-data-performance.md#q018)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S03-Q018](../../sources/03-sql-data-performance.md#q018)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain database concurrency.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Concurrency is overlapping progress, not merely many users. Trace the possible interleavings and identify which outcome violates the business rule.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Recognize a concurrency problem from an execution sequence.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>State the reads, writes and invariant for one SQL Server database. Do not assume that transactions alone provide every required concurrency guarantee.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Shows a specific interleaving and the resulting state rather than naming races abstractly.</li>
<li>Distinguishes correctness requirements from waiting and throughput requirements.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Saying concurrent access is safe simply because each request uses a transaction.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would you reproduce the unsafe interleaving with two database sessions?</li>
</ul>

</details>

### S03-Q020 · Mechanism

<p>Explain row versioning in SQL Server. Which reader/writer interaction are you discussing, and what is the relevant consistency boundary?</p>

**Source:** [S03-Q020](../../sources/03-sql-data-performance.md#q020)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S03-Q020](../../sources/03-sql-data-performance.md#q020)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain row versioning.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Describe what a reader sees as data changes and distinguish this mechanism from an application concurrency token. The source term needs a precise context.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Explain versioned reads without confusing different uses of &#x27;version&#x27;.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Specify SQL Server version, isolation mode and database configuration. Verify behavior and version-storage requirements in official documentation; do not assume defaults.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Traces two overlapping sessions and identifies the reader&#x27;s view of data.</li>
<li>Discusses write conflicts and resource/lifetime boundaries for the chosen mode.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Equating row versioning with the rowversion data type or claiming it eliminates all blocking.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

### S03-Q021 · Mechanism

<p>Compare common transaction isolation levels using a concrete read/write sequence. Which consistency property and cost would drive your choice?</p>

**Source:** [S03-Q021](../../sources/03-sql-data-performance.md#q021)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Isolation describes how overlapping transactions may affect what is observed. Explain the difference through outcomes, not only the names of levels.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Connect an isolation choice to a required observable guarantee.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Specify SQL Server version, database options and transaction boundaries. Check official behavior for locking or versioned modes before claiming defaults or supported guarantees.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>

<li>Explains the cost and a two-session test that distinguishes the alternatives.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Choosing the strongest-sounding name without identifying the anomaly the business must prevent.</li>
</ul>

<a id="S03-Q023"></a>

### S03-Q023 · Failure cases

<p>What is a database deadlock? Illustrate the dependency that makes it different from ordinary blocking.</p>

**Source:** [S03-Q023](../../sources/03-sql-data-performance.md#q023)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S03-Q023](../../sources/03-sql-data-performance.md#q023)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> What is a deadlock?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Trace two or more operations waiting on resources. Make clear why the system cannot resolve that particular wait by simply letting one holder continue normally.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Recognize a deadlock from its resource and wait relationships.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Use a small SQL Server transaction example and state the resources involved. Separate deadlock, prolonged blocking and timeout symptoms.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Draws or describes a complete wait cycle with owners and requested resources.</li>
<li>Explains which observation distinguishes the cycle from a one-way wait.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Calling every slow or blocked query a deadlock without establishing a cycle.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What evidence would you request before accepting a report that a timeout was caused by a deadlock?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S03-Q024"></a>

### S03-Q024 · Failure cases

<p>How would you diagnose a recurring SQL Server deadlock and connect it to the application operations that created it?</p>

**Source:** [S03-Q024](../../sources/03-sql-data-performance.md#q024)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S03-Q024](../../sources/03-sql-data-performance.md#q024)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> How would you diagnose the root cause of a deadlock?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Reconstruct the conflicting resource acquisition from evidence. Separate the session selected as the victim from the underlying cause of the cycle.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Turn a deadlock report into a testable root-cause explanation.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Specify the deployed SQL Server version and available capture tooling; verify documented collection behavior. No particular graph, plan or incident is supplied here.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Identifies owners, waiters, statements and transaction boundaries from diagnostic evidence.</li>
<li>Proposes a reproduction and evidence that could disprove the suspected cause.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Blaming the victim alone or changing isolation without reconstructing the conflicting operations.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What information would you need if the application logs contain only the victim&#x27;s error?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S03-Q019"></a>

### S03-Q019 · Trade-offs

<p>For competing updates to the same business record, how would you choose between optimistic concurrency and pessimistic locking?</p>

**Source:** [S03-Q019](../../sources/03-sql-data-performance.md#q019)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S03-Q019](../../sources/03-sql-data-performance.md#q019)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Compare optimistic concurrency and pessimistic locking.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Compare when conflicts are dealt with and what the caller must do afterward. Give the workload condition that favors each approach.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Choose concurrency control from conflict rates and required behavior.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>State the invariant, transaction duration and expected contention. Name the concrete conflict-detection or locking mechanism rather than relying on the labels alone.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Traces a conflict through the chosen mechanism and the application response.</li>
<li>Explains retry, waiting and resource costs with a condition that changes the choice.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Calling optimistic control lock-free or ignoring failed updates and retry limits.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would your choice change if conflicts become frequent during a traffic spike?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S03-Q022"></a>

### S03-Q022 · Trade-offs

<p>How could strengthening transaction isolation change blocking and throughput? Explain how you would assess the impact on a real workload.</p>

**Source:** [S03-Q022](../../sources/03-sql-data-performance.md#q022)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S03-Q022](../../sources/03-sql-data-performance.md#q022)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> How do higher isolation levels affect blocking and throughput?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Relate a consistency decision to interactions between concurrent requests. Distinguish possible costs from effects you have actually measured.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Evaluate isolation&#x27;s workload consequences without oversimplifying them.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Specify SQL Server version, isolation implementation, configuration and transaction duration; check official behavior. A higher level does not imply one universal performance ranking.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Explains which overlapping operations could wait or conflict under the selected modes.</li>
<li>Compares correctness, waits, throughput and resource use under representative contention.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Saying &#x27;higher isolation is always slower&#x27; without naming the modes, workload or measurements.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<a id="S03-Q025"></a>

### S03-Q025 · Trade-offs

<p>Once you understand a deadlock cycle, how would you reduce its probability without weakening the required correctness?</p>

**Source:** [S03-Q025](../../sources/03-sql-data-performance.md#q025)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S03-Q025](../../sources/03-sql-data-performance.md#q025)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> How would you reduce deadlock probability?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Choose a change that addresses the demonstrated conflict. Explain which part of the cycle changes and what new cost or limitation the change introduces.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Design a targeted deadlock reduction and validate its trade-offs.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>State the resource cycle, business invariant and representative contention. Reducing probability is not a promise that every deadlock disappears.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Connects the proposed change to resource order, transaction duration or the demonstrated access pattern.</li>
<li>Tests concurrency and correctness while retaining a safe application recovery path.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Applying a blanket hint or isolation change without proving it addresses this cycle.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would you verify the fix if the original deadlock appears only under load?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S03-Q026"></a>

### S03-Q026 · Production decision

<p>When SQL Server selects a transaction as a deadlock victim, how should its application caller recover safely?</p>

**Source:** [S03-Q026](../../sources/03-sql-data-performance.md#q026)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S03-Q026](../../sources/03-sql-data-performance.md#q026)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> How should applications respond when SQL Server selects a deadlock victim?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Trace database state, application state and the decision to retry or report failure. The question concerns safe recovery as well as identifying the error.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Design a bounded, observable recovery path for a failed transaction.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Specify SQL Server and .NET provider versions; confirm documented error and transaction behavior. State any external effects and whether the business operation can be retried.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Identifies the retry unit and prevents incomplete or duplicated business effects.</li>
<li>Defines retry limits, user-visible outcome and telemetry for repeated failures.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Retrying one statement blindly or looping indefinitely without considering the whole operation.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would recovery change if the operation had already called an external service?</li>
</ul>

</details>

## Combined production exercise — agent-added

<p>Two .NET worker replicas allocate the last available stock while another request reads availability. Define the invariant, choose a control strategy and a SQL Server isolation/configuration scope to verify. Describe two-session tests, then a deadlock involving two stock records; specify diagnostic evidence, a targeted reduction and a bounded retry/reporting contract, including any external effects.</p>

## Short rubric — use only with an actual attempt

**Basic answer**

<p>Explains transaction outcomes and recognizes a conflicting update or deadlock cycle.</p>

**Senior answer**

<p>Defends guarantees from an execution trace, verifies configuration, diagnoses the actual cycle and preserves the invariant through retries and failure reporting.</p>

**Still needs evidence**

<p>No interleaving, database configuration, test output or diagnostic artifact is supplied; the claimed concurrency guarantee remains unproven.</p>
